- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.75) and underestimates when sentiment is low (<0.3).
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if recent history shows a sharp drop, forecast should not immediately rebound; allow 2–3 periods for price to stabilize before predicting new highs.
- Suppress overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a sharp rise following a spike (e.g., >70), reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Adjust for sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.6), model tends to overpredict; when sentiment is falling (e.g., <0.4), underpredict — apply sentiment-weighted correction (e.g., +0.5% for sentiment >0.7, -0.5% for <0.3).
- Avoid horizon-specific overfitting: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) — reduce initial forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
